extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars and practitioners of psychoanalysis, psychology, and humor theory
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical criteria and techniques describing how jokes are formed and why they produce pleasure, framed in psychoanalytic terms (condensation, displacement, unconscious revision) and contrasted with dream-work. Useful for analyzing or producing jokes from a psychoanalytic perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of repeating a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Telling my joke to another person would seem to serve several purposes: first, to give me objective certainty that the joke-work has been successful; secondly, to complete my own pleasure by a reaction from the other person upon myself; and thirdly ... to make up for the loss of pleasure owing to the joke’s lack of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating the social function of joke-telling include: (1) verification of success, (2) augmentation/completion of pleasure via others' reactions, and (3) compensation when the joke is not novel (repetition restores some pleasure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychical economy (localized economy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original yield of pleasure... was derived from mere economy in expenditure; but with the development of play into a joke the tendency to economy too must alter its aims... A localized economy, such as we have just been considering, will not fail to give us momentary pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess jokes for signs of 'economy' in the sense of saving psychical/inhibitory expenditure (e.g., concise substitutions, re-use of material). Note that economy here is not mere brevity but a pleasure-yielding saving of a familiar expenditure; localized economies give momentary pleasure but may not produce lasting relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief through discharge (general relief)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is only if this disposal elsewhere can be avoided that this specialized economy is transformed into a general relief of psychical expenditure... the factor of relief takes the place of economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a joke produces not just a local economy but a sense of 'relief' — reduction of inhibition or discharge of psychical energy. In jokes this relief often results via the joke's interpersonal unfolding (first person to third person) and gives a greater feeling of pleasure than mere economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the course of the dream-work the material of the dream-thoughts is subjected to a quite extraordinary compression or condensation... newly-created common elements of condensation enter the manifest content ... an element in the dream corresponds to a nodal point or junction in the dream-thoughts, and ... is ‘overdetermined’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat condensation as a central joke technique: multiple latent thoughts/associations are compressed into a single joke element (word, image, turn). Look for overlaps, double meanings, puns, and compressed nodal points that carry intensified cathexis; condensation explains brevity and multilayered significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement (dream-displacement analogues)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second great modification ... 'dream-displacement' ... things that lie on the periphery of the dream-thoughts and are of minor importance occupy a central position... the dream-work ... displacement ... is the diversion of cathectic energy from important to unimportant ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In jokes displacement appears as substitution of an objectionable idea by a peripheral/innocent one (analogy, symbol, remote allusion). While displacement is more pervasive in dreams, assess jokes for displacement when inhibition must be evaded — especially in tendentious or socially risky jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect representation (allusion, symbolism, analogy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Among displacements are ... every sort of indirect representation as well, and in particular the replacement of an important but objectionable element by one that is indifferent ... substitution by a piece of symbolism, or an analogy, or something small.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of indirect devices to veil an intended target: successful jokes often use allusion/symbolism/analogy to make objectionable content passable to the 'censorship' (audience norms). Distinguish deliberate rhetorical allusion (conscious) from unconscious indirect representation typical of joke-work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity ('joking' brevity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke’s brevity is of a peculiar kind - ‘joking’ brevity... the brevity of jokes, like that of dreams, would be a necessary concomitant of the condensations which occur in both of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the economy of a joke not by general concision but by its 'joking' brevity: the terse form that reflects condensation and heightened intensity. Mere shortness is not sufficient; the brevity should reflect condensed multilayer meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntariness / sudden emergence
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke has quite outstandingly the characteristic of being a notion that has occurred to us ‘involuntarily’... we have an indefinable feeling... and then all at once the joke is there - as a rule ready-clothed in words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for spontaneity as a sign of authentic joke-work: jokes that feel 'sudden' or emergent (vs. consciously crafted witticisms) align with unconscious revision processes. Distinguish between deliberately planned allusions and jokes that arise involuntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association behavior and memory accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes show a special way of behaving, too, in regard to association. Often they are not at the disposal of our memory when we want them; but at other times ... they appear involuntarily ... at points in our train of thought where we cannot see their relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing joke production, note that jokes may be inaccessible on demand yet spontaneously appear in unrelated contexts — this associative unpredictability supports an unconscious origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of occasion and ambiguity to evade inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes do not, like dreams, create compromises; they do not evade the inhibition, but they insist on maintaining play with words or with nonsense unaltered. They restrict themselves, however, to a choice of occasions in which this play or this nonsense can at the same time appear allowable (in jests) or sensible (in jokes), thanks to the ambiguity of words and the multiplicity of conceptual relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate situational appropriateness: effective jokes exploit contexts where ambiguity or duplicity renders playful/nonsensical content allowable. The selection of occasion is part of successful joke technique to bypass censorship without altering the play itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play upon words / multiple use / similarity of sound
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the outcomes of condensation - multiple use of the same material, play upon words, and similarity of sound - ... the original intention of jokes was to obtain a yield of pleasure of this kind from words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify linguistic devices (puns, homophony, repetition) that enable condensed multiple-meaning effects. These devices are primary sources of pleasure in jokes and are often produced by the unconscious condensations Freud describes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendentious jokes and double inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest stage of jokes, tendentious jokes, often have to overcome two kinds of inhibition, those opposed to the joke itself and those opposed to its purpose ... allusions and displacements are well qualified to make this latter task possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For politically/socially charged (tendentious) humor, evaluate how the joke negotiates both: (a) inhibition against joking form and (b) inhibition against the joke's hostile or aggressive purpose. Use of allusion/displacement/symbolism indicates techniques to surmount these dual barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of regression to perception in jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no doubt that the regression of the train of thought to perception is absent in jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike dreams, jokes do not undergo 'regression' (conversion of wish into hallucinatory perceptual 'It is'). When analyzing joke-formation, do not expect pictorial regression; focus instead on condensation and selective displacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconscious origin and infantile thought-style
rubrics_metrics.description: The thought which, with the intention of constructing a joke, plunges into the unconscious is merely seeking there for the ancient dwelling-place of its former play with words. Thought is put back for a moment to the stage of childhood so as once more to gain possession of the childish source of pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the 'infantile' quality in jokes: childish play with words and simplistic logical operations often reappear. Successful jokes may exploit this reversion to childhood modes of thought, which are preserved in the unconscious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overdetermination of joke elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The newly-created common elements of condensation enter the manifest content ... an element in the dream corresponds to a nodal point or junction in the dream-thoughts, and, as compared with these latter, must quite generally be described as ‘overdetermined’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether joke elements carry multiple, independent associative determinants (overdetermination). Overdetermined elements are rich signifiers that link to various latent thoughts and increase the joke's density and pleasure-yield.
